title: Convert Speed to $$\frac{m}{s}$$
text: First, convert the initial speed from $$\frac{km}{h}$$ to $$\frac{m}{s}$$. Remember that $$1\, \tfrac{\text{km}}{\text{hr}}$$ is equal to 1/$$3.6\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$.

title: Calculate Initial Speed in $$\frac{m}{s}$$
text: Use the conversion factor to find the initial speed in $$\frac{m}{s}$$. What is $$1000\, \tfrac{\text{km}}{\text{hr}}$$ in $$\frac{m}{s}$$?

title: Initial Speed in $$\frac{m}{s}$$
text: Calculate the initial speed in $$\frac{m}{s}$$ using the conversion factor.

title: Use the Formula for Acceleration
text: The formula for acceleration is $$a=(v_{f}-v_{i})/t$$, $$where$$ $$v_{f}$$ is the final velocity, $$v_{i}$$ is the initial velocity, and $$t$$ is the time.

title: Calculate Acceleration
text: Substitute the values into the formula: $$v_{f}=0\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$, $$v_{i}=277.78\,\tfrac{\text{m}}{\text{s}}$$, $$and$$ $$t=1.10\, \text{s}$$.
